title: A user id in a request names the caller, or the request is refused
description: About twenty routes take a user id, in the path of the aliases jellyfin-web calls or in a userId query, and ignore it: the answer is the caller's data whatever the id says (routes.go:121, items.go:67). Nothing leaks, but an administrator who asks for another user's list is given their own under the other's name, and no test would notice a handler that started to honour the id without a check. Two handlers that do honour it carry two hand-written copies of the check, in two orders (sessions.go:346-372, user_configuration.go:160-175). This task makes one rule, in one place, before any handler runs.
acceptanceCriteria: Observed first, the main matrix: compat/captures/user-scope-12.4.md and .json record what jellyfin/jellyfin:12.4 does for every route in compat/endpoints.yaml, with an administrator and two non-administrators A and B, each holding data that tells them apart (a favourite, a played item, display preferences, a Configuration, a session). For each route: the status and whose data came back or changed (A, B, the administrator, nobody, or "not a Jellyfin route").

The cases in that matrix: A names B in the {userId} path segment; A names B as userId in the query; A names an id that is no user; A names a malformed id; A names its own id dashed and in upper case; the administrator names B, an id that is no user, and a malformed id; the all-zero id is named.
The capture also records POST /Items/{itemId}/PlaybackInfo with UserId in its body, and GET /Sessions with controllableByUserId, for the same callers and ids.

A script under test/differential/ (capture_user_scope.py, after capture_access.py and capture_user_configuration.py) makes the capture and can be run again from the repository root; the /jellyscale/v1/ routes are recorded as not a Jellyfin route.

Route has Users: 'own' (the default) or 'admin-any'. 'admin-any' is exactly GET /Users/{userId}, POST /Users/Configuration, POST /Users/{userId}/Configuration and POST /UserItems/{itemId}/UserData; every other viewer route is 'own'.

--print-routes writes user: on every route that is not 'anyone' and on no 'anyone' route; compat/endpoints.yaml is regenerated, and docs/access.md's Scope column agrees with Users for every route (by review, not by a test).

On every 'own' route one guard, before the handler, answers 403 when any of these names anyone but the caller: the {userId} path segment; any userId query value; any controllableByUserId query value; UserId in the body of POST /Items/{itemId}/PlaybackInfo or POST /jellyscale/v1/items/{itemId}/playback-info. It holds for a non-administrator and an administrator alike.
On 'own' routes the 403 has the same status and body whether the id is another user's, nobody's or malformed.

Every value counts: ?userId=<A>&userId=<B>, ?userId=<A>&UserId=<B>, A's id in the path with B's in the query, and A's id in the query with B's in the PlaybackInfo body all answer 403, and the guard does not use up PlaybackInfo's body before the handler reads it.

A refused request does nothing: it sends Postgres no statement beyond the token lookup and changes no row of B's or of the caller's. After POST /Sessions/Logout?userId=<B> A's token still works; after POST /UserPlayedItems/{id}?userId=<B> A's played state is unchanged; after DELETE /Videos/ActiveEncodings?userId=<B> A's job is still running; GET /socket?userId=<B> gets no 101.

The caller's own id, dashed or compact, lower or upper case, in any of the four places, answers exactly as the request without it (same status and body); a PlaybackInfo whose body has A's UserId and a profile that forces a transcode gets the same transcode as without it; an empty userId= counts as no id.
Authentication comes first: a request naming B with no token or an unknown token gets 401 unauthorized, never 403.
The guard holds on a process with the api role alone, the stream role alone, and both.

While Postgres is away, on a snapshot route, a request naming B is never served from the snapshot, a request with no user id is served from it as today, and no request is answered 4xx because Postgres is away (invariant 37).
On an 'admin-any' route a non-administrator naming another user's id, or a well-formed id of nobody, gets 403 with the same status and body, and no statement beyond the token lookup is sent.
On an 'admin-any' route a malformed id gets 400 whoever asks, including GET /Users/{malformed} and GET /Users/Configuration, which the {userId} pattern matches.

On an 'admin-any' route an administrator naming a user acts on that user only: GET /Users/{B} returns B's record; a Configuration write naming B changes B's row and none of the administrator's; a UserData write naming B does the same.
On an 'admin-any' route an administrator naming a well-formed id of nobody gets 404 and nothing is written.

Where the path and the query of one 'admin-any' request name different users, a non-administrator gets 403 as for any other user's id, and an administrator gets 400 and nothing is read or written (the lead's addition; Jellyfin's behaviour in the capture is recorded, and it is a difference named in docs/access.md if it differs).
One helper makes the 'admin-any' decision: getUser (users.go), userDataTarget (sessions.go) and saveConfiguration (user_configuration.go) hold no copy of the check.

TestAccess makes A, B and an administrator by SQL and asks every viewer route with B's id in every place the route can take one (path where it has {userId}; userId and controllableByUserId in the query on every route; the body of the two PlaybackInfo POSTs): with A's token 403 on every route; with the administrator's token 403 on every 'own' route; on each of the three handlers of criterion 13.
With the administrator's token and B's id, GET /Users/{B} returns B's record and each of the three admin-any writes lands on B.
After A's sweep and the administrator's sweep of the 'own' routes, every row of B's is byte for byte what it was: users, user_item_data, display_preferences, sessions, devices and session_sockets.

Every 'anyone' route asked with userId=<B>, with no token and with A's token, answers as without the id; POST /Users/AuthenticateByName?userId=<B> with A's name and password signs in A (User.Id is A's).

Named mutants, each failing every run, each shown once by hand in the Spec step and recorded (D-069), none committed: the guard reads the path and not the query; the guard lets an administrator through on an 'own' route; the helper looks the user up before it refuses a non-administrator (as saveConfiguration does today); the guard reads only the first userId value; the guard compares a query id with its letter case.

The JS-116 replay: exactly one case changes and the pull request names it. A non-administrator naming an id that is no user on the three Configuration routes got 404, as on Jellyfin, and now gets 403 so the answer no longer says whether the id is a user. expectedOf in cmd/jellyscale/user_configuration_integration_test.go and the capture file's 'What the replay holds jellyscale to' are amended for that case alone, citing D-075 (the lead's record of the owner's access decision of 2026-11-16). Every other case passes unchanged.

Changed answers listed in the pull request: a request naming another user's id got 200 with the caller's data and now gets 403 (internal/api/playback_integration_test.go lines 657 to 700, which send /Users/{other}/PlayedItems and FavoriteItems and expect the caller's data, are corrected by the lead); GET /Users/{malformed} got 403 or 404 and now gets 400. Neither is visible to a viewer using a client, which sends its own id.

The all-zero id is refused (403 on 'own' routes) as 'not the caller's'. If the capture shows Jellyfin serving it and the capture of a supported client shows it sending one, that returns to the product owner as a trade-off brief, not a quiet relaxation.
jellyfin-web still works: the e2e tier passes unchanged and the differential tier passes with no new entry.

The docs say the new rule: DOMAINS.md invariant 49 and the routes.go comment 'These act on the caller whatever userId says'; docs/access.md line 15 and line 33 (which says a test holds its table to the capture, and none does); docs/api.md lines 7 and 48 (which say the namespace ignores userId); and, under 'Stricter than Jellyfin' in docs/access.md, a row saying an administrator is served another user's view on four routes only, citing the capture entry that shows Jellyfin serving it everywhere.
notes: Changed answers, to list in the pull request: a request naming another user's id got 200 with the caller's data and now gets 403; the Configuration 404 above. Neither is visible to a viewer using a client, which always sends its own id.Tests make their second user by SQL, as user_configuration_integration_test.go does; no seeding route is added. Jellyfin's rule is RequestHelpers.GetUserId (Jellyfin.Api/Helpers/RequestHelpers.cs:67-81 at v12.4). Owner's decisions (2026-11-16, on Fable 5.2's access model, .results/access-model-fable-2026-11-16.md): pictures by id open to whoever holds the id, by name need a token; per-library access right after JS-033; a revoked or disabled user's running stream stops within 15 s; a viewer sees no other viewer's name; an administrator manages accounts but never browses, plays or reports as another user; a Policy field jellyscale does not enforce is refused when changed (400); 'may download' is honoured; operator keys are never users; no issue is filed on Findroid for now. D-069: named mutants are shown failing once by hand in the Spec step and recorded in the task's record; no mutant table or script is committed.
